110006.text: The Strange Behaviour Of Captain Van Toch
110006.com: FCB: I fixed the DB, so it is a little strange, don't worry about it.

110007.text: If you looked up the little island of Tana Masa on the map you would find it just on the Equator, not far south of Sumatra; but if you were on the deck of the Kandong Bandoeng and asked its captain, J. van Toch, what he thought of this Tana Masa where you’ve just dropped anchor he would first curse for a short while and then he would tell you that it’s the dirtiest hole all the Sunda Islands, even more loathsome than Tana Bala and easily as damnable as Pini or Banyak; that the only apology for a human being that lives there — not counting these louse-ridden Bataks, of course — is a drunken commercial agent, a cross between a Cuban and a Portuguese, and an even bigger thief, pagan and pig than the whole of Cuba and the whole of the white race put together; if there’s anything in this world that’s damnable then it’s the damned life on this damned Tana Masa.

110008.text: And then, you might cautiously ask him why it is that he’s just dropped his damned anchor as if he wanted to spend three damned days here; at which he would snort in irritation and grumble something about not being so damned stupid as to sail all the way to Kandon Bandoeng just to get this damned copra or palm oil, and there’s nothing else here, but I’ve got my damned orders, and you will please be so kind as to mind your own damned business.

110009.text: And he would carry on cursing as widely and as fully as you might expect from a sea captain who was no longer young but still lively for his age.

110010.text: But if, instead of asking all sorts of impertinent questions, you left Captain J. van Toch to grumble and curse by himself you might find out something more.

110011.text: Surely it’s obvious the man needs a rest.

110012.text: Just leave him alone, he can sort out his foul mood by himself.

110015.text: “Those damned Jew-boys back in Amsterdam, all they seem to think about is pearls.

110016.text: Have a look around you; can you see any pearls?

110017.text: They say the people are crazy round here for pearls and that sort of thing.”

110018.text: At this point the captain spat in anger.

110019.text: “We know all about that, load up with pearls!

110020.text: That’s because you people always want to start a war or something.

110021.text: All you’re worried about is money.

110022.text: And then you call it a crisis.”

110023.text: For a short while, Captain J. van Toch considered whether he ought to start discussing political economics, considering that that’s all they ever do talk about nowadays.

110024.text: But it’s too hot and languid to talk about that sort of thing here, anchored off Tana Masa; so the captain merely waved his hand and grumbled: “That’s what they say, pearls!

110025.text: In Ceylon they’ve got enough pearls piled up to last them for five years, on Formosa they’ve put a ban on gathering them — and so they say to me, Captain van Toch, go and see if you can find somewhere new to gather pearls.

110026.text: Go on down to those damned little islands, you might find whole bays full of oysters down there …”

110027.text: The captain pulled out his light-blue handkerchief and blew his nose in contempt.

110028.text: “Those rats in Europe, they think there’s still something to find down here, something they don’t already know about.

110029.text: God, what a bunch of fools they are!

110030.text: Next they’ll be wanting me to look up the Bataks snouts to see if they don’t have them full of pearls.

110032.text: I know there’s a new brothel in Padang, but new pearl fisheries?

110033.text: I know these islands like my trousers, all the way from Ceylon down to that damned Clipperton Island, and if anyone thinks there’s anything new still left to find there that they can make any money out of, well good luck to them.

110034.text: Thirty years I’ve been sailing these waters, and now these fools think I’m going to discover something new!”

110035.text: This was a task so insulting it made Captain van Toch gasp.

110036.text: “Why can’t they send some green kid to find something for them if they want to gape in astonishment; but instead they expect someone to do that who knows the area as well as Captain J. van Toch … Please try and understand this.

110037.text: In Europe there might still be something left to discover; but here — people only come here to sniff out something they could eat, or rather not even to eat, to find something to buy and sell.

110038.text: If in all these damned tropics there was still something they could double the price of there’d be three commercial agents standing there waving their snotty handkerchiefs at the ships of seven countries to stop for it.

110040.text: I know about these things better than the colonial office of Her Majesty the Queen, if you’ll forgive me.”

110041.text: Captain van Toch made a great effort to overcome his righteous indignation, and after a prolonged period of exertion he was successful.

110042.text: “D’you see those two contemptible layabouts down there?

110043.text: They’re pearl fishers from Ceylon, Sinhalese, God help us, just as the Lord made them; but what He made them for, I don’t know.

110044.text: I have them on board with me, and when we find any stretch of coast that doesn’t have a sign up saying Agency or Bata or Customs Office down they go in the water to look for oysters.

110045.text: That small bugger, he can dive down eighty meters deep; in the Princes Islands he went down to ninety meters to get the handle from a film projector.

110050.text: And that’s the sort of worthless work I do.

110051.text: Pretend to be buying palm oil and all the time looking for new pearl fisheries.

110052.text: Next they’ll be wanting me to find a new virgin continent for them.

110053.text: This isn’t a job for an honest captain in the merchant navy.

110054.text: Captain J. van Toch isn’t some cursed adventurer, no.

110055.text: And on he would go; the sea is wide and the ocean of time has no limits; spit in the sea, my friend, and it will not return, berate your destiny and you will never change it; and so on through many preparations and circumstances until we finally arrive at the point when J. van Toch, captain of the Dutch vessel, Kandong Bandoeng, will sigh and climb down into the boat for the trip to Tana Masa where he will negotiate with the drunken half-cast of Cubanese and Portuguese extraction about certain business matters.

110056.text: “Sorry, Captain,” the half-cast of Cubanese and Portuguese extraction finally said, “but here on Tana Masa there aren’t any oysters.

110057.text: These filthy Bataks,” he would inform him with boundless disgust, “will even eat the jellyfish; there are more of them in the water than on the land, the women here smell of fish, you cannot imagine what it is like — what was I saying?

110058.text: Ah, yes, you were asking about women.”

110059.text: “And is there not even any stretch of coastline round here,” the captain asked, “where these Bataks don’t go in the water?”

110060.text: The half-cast of Cubanese and Portuguese shook his head.

110062.text: Unless you count Devil Bay, but that would not interest you.”

110064.text: “Because … no-one is allowed to go there.

110068.text: “Sharks and everything else besides,” the half-cast mumbled.

110070.text: The Bataks would not like to see anyone going down there.”

110076.text: “Not a fish,” the half-cast corrected him.

110081.text: They say that that’s where they have their city, these demons.

110083.text: “And what do they look like, these sea demons?”

110084.text: The half cast of Cubanese and Portuguese shrugged his shoulders.

110086.text: I once saw one of them … or just its head, at least.

110087.text: I was coming back in a boat from Cape Haarlem … and suddenly, in front of me, a kind of lump stuck up out of the water.”

110089.text: “It had a head … like a Batak, Captain, but entirely without hair.”

110092.text: In this place no Batak would ever go into the water.

110093.text: And then … the thing blinked at me with an eyelid from beneath its eye.”

110094.text: The half-cast shuddered with the horror of it.

110095.text: “An eyelid from beneath its eye, which reached up to cover the whole eye.

110097.text: Captain J. van Toch turned his glass of palm wine around between his chubby fingers.

110098.text: “And you hadn’t been drinking, had you?

110101.text: How else would I ever had rowed into that place.
